title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: a local analysis at a 'point' x within Grothendieck's Teichmüller-groupoid programme (the continuation of La Longue Marche). The notation suggests the following, though it is my reading. $\mathbb{S}_x$ is a circle (a small loop around x). $D^*_x$ is a punctured disc at x. $\underline{A}_x$ is a category of local data at x (perhaps tangential base points or 'amorces'). $\underline{\mathrm{Gr}}(\underline{A}_x)$ is the groupoid obtained by inverting all arrows of $\underline{A}_x$. $T=T_x$ is the commutative fundamental group, ≅ Z.

The previous page establishes three things. First, $\underline{\mathrm{Gr}}(\underline{A}_x)$ is equivalent to the groupoid of universal coverings of $\mathbb{S}_x$. Second, the functor $\underline{\mathrm{Gr}}(H)$ is essentially constant. Third, the values $H(A)$ are therefore linked by a transitive system of isomorphisms. Their common value is written $H(\tilde{\mathbb{S}}_x,\tilde D^*_x)$; it depends only on the chosen universal covers.

On this page:
- **(107)** expresses compatibility of the identifications $i_A$ with the transition isomorphisms (100), as a commutative triangle.
- **(108)–(109)** prove essential constancy. Two functors, $A\mapsto\tilde{\mathbb{S}}_{x,A}$ and $A\mapsto \tilde D^*_{x,A}$, go into the coverings of $\mathbb{S}_x$ and of $D^*_x$. Each factors through $\underline{\mathrm{Gr}}(\underline{A}_x)$ as an equivalence of groupoids, F and G.
- **(110)**: after fixing $\tilde{\mathbb{S}}$ and $\tilde D^*$, the relevant torsors are $\mathrm{Isom}(F(A),\tilde{\mathbb S})$ and $\mathrm{Isom}(G(A),\tilde D^*)$. These are functorial in A and extend to $\underline{\mathrm{Gr}}$ by its universal property.
- **Abstraction (finished on the next page).** Let T be commutative and let $\mathcal G,\mathcal G',\mathcal G''$ be connected T-groupoids, i.e. groupoids whose automorphism groups are identified compatibly with T. Let $F:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ and $G:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G''$ be T-equivalences, and fix objects X', X''. Then $X\mapsto \mathrm{Isom}_T(\mathrm{Hom}(F X,X'),\mathrm{Hom}(G X,X''))$ is a constant functor into T-torsors. Proof: via quasi-inverses this is $\mathrm{Isom}_T(\mathrm{Hom}(X,F_1X'),\mathrm{Hom}(X,G_1X''))$, which is $\cong \mathrm{Hom}(F_1X',G_1X'')$ by composition, independently of X.

The purpose is to define canonically a T-torsor comparing the universal covers of the circle and of the punctured disc, independent of the auxiliary choice A. This is a standard 'canonical object by transitive system' construction.
errors: (110), second line: the argument written as $D_x^{*\sim}(E_x A)$ looks like a slip or abbreviation; by analogy with the first line it should simply be a function of A.
On the next page the quasi-inverse of G is named $G_1$ in (114) but $F_2$ in (115)–(116); this is a notational inconsistency only.

The argument implicitly needs T commutative and the T-structures preserved by F and G, so that composition gives a T-equivariant identification. The text asserts this ('groupe commutatif T') rather than checking it. The conclusion is correct.

ideas.what: Defining an object canonically as the common value of an essentially constant functor on a connected groupoid (transitive system of isomorphisms)
ideas.modern_name: limit/colimit of a functor on a connected (simply connected) groupoid; canonical identification by transitive systems

ideas.what: Groupoid of local data at x equivalent to the groupoid of universal coverings of the circle / punctured disc
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points and the local fundamental groupoid at a puncture
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tangential base points informally; La Longue Marche (unpublished)

ideas.what: Lemma: for equivalences of connected T-groupoids (T commutative), Isom of the Hom-torsors to fixed targets is independent of the source object
ideas.modern_name: banded groupoids / T-gerbes over a point; torsor calculus

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping of canonical identifications (torsors between universal covers of circle and punctured disc) inside the Teichmüller-groupoid project; the abstract lemma is elementary torsor/gerbe calculus.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Pour vérifier le fait que le foncteur Gr(H) de (102) est ...' reads 'est ess. constant' (essentiellement constant), not 'est une équivalence'.
The parenthetical reads '(indépendants du choix de $\tilde{\mathbb S}_x$, $\tilde D^*_x$)'.

Final lines read roughly: 'et ces isom. fonctoriels s'étendent sur la catégorie Gr(A_x). Dans la situation abstraite, on a un groupe commutatif T (=T_x), trois T-groupoïdes connexes $\mathcal G,\mathcal G',\mathcal G''$'.

(110), first line: the left side looks like $H(A)$ or $\tilde{\mathbb S}(A)$ (a struck letter is overwritten). The subscript under Isom is 'Revêt($\mathbb S_x$)', with $F(A)=\tilde{\mathbb S}_{x,A}$ indicated by an underbrace.
